attack_surfaces: Agent memory; pairwise inter-agent communication.

canonical_title: Breaking and Fixing Defenses Against Control-Flow Hijacking in Multi-Agent Systems

canonical_title: When Embedding-Based Defenses Fail: Rethinking Safety in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
canonical_authors: Lingxi Zhang; Guangtao Zheng; Hanjie Chen

canonical_title: When collaboration fails: persuasion driven adversarial influence in multi agent large language model debate
canonical_authors: Insaf Kraidia; Iyas Qaddara; Alhanof Almutairi; Nada Alzaben; Samir Brahim Belhouari
version_status: Published open-access journal article, 8 April 2026.
identity_verdict: Title, five-author list, publication date, journal volume/article number, and DOI verified on the Nature publisher page.
scope_rationale: Intentional malicious-member persuasion alters a collective decision through explicit inter-agent deliberation; this is not merely generic performance degradation.
multiagent_verdict: Yes. One or more adversarial debate members observe prior arguments and influence cooperative agents across repeated debate rounds and majority aggregation.
adversary_position: Malicious member inside an otherwise cooperative debate group.
adversary_capabilities: Read full debate history; promote a designated target; generate multi-layer arguments, rebuttals, fused narratives, Best-of-N candidates, and RAG-supported rhetoric.
preconditions: All participants consume a shared transcript; a final decision is produced by debate/majority; the controlled evaluation assigns a wrong target for reproducible measurement.
mechanism: Inference-time adaptive persuasion and contextual accumulation, optionally strengthened by RAG and Best-of-N selection.
attack_surfaces: Peer messages; shared debate transcript; majority-vote aggregation.
primary_system_failure: Collective decision-integrity failure.
reported_impact: Reduced group answer accuracy and increased agreement with the attacker-selected wrong answer; no real-world downstream action is executed.
agent_count_or_configuration: Multiple cooperative agents plus one or more adversarial agents; exact group sizes vary by experiment and should be extracted per table rather than reduced to one number.
topology: Multi-round debate with shared peer responses and final selection/majority vote.
communication: All agents receive the common question and later peer responses; the attacker adapts to previous rounds.
baselines: Honest debate, lower-capability/vanilla adversary, variations in group size and rounds, and prompt-warning mitigation.
metric_definition: Two-part outcome: drop in final group accuracy and rise in the fraction of agents agreeing with the adversarial target; paper also reports setting-specific accuracy/consensus changes.
unit_denominator: Question/debate-instance level for final accuracy plus agent-within-round agreement fractions; the headline 10–40% and >30% are ranges across evaluated settings, not one universal effect.
system_level_impact_verified: Yes for benchmark-level collective decision corruption; no external environment action or deployed-system consequence was tested.
evidence_locators: Publisher HTML: abstract and Threat model & Attack design; paper pp. 4-5 Fig. 1/Algorithm 1; pp. 10-11 setup/metrics; pp. 14-16 Figs. 11-13 for mitigation.
author_claim_vs_corpus_interpretation: Authors explicitly frame persuasion as an adversarial vector and report benchmark effects. Coding it as collective decision integrity, rather than a separate “persuasion risk,” is the corpus interpretation.
limitations_maturity: Peer-reviewed journal evidence. Controlled wrong-target assignment, benchmark QA/voting outcomes, model- and prompt-dependent effect sizes, and prompt-only mitigation limit generalization.
key_corrections: Retain as attack-primary; record the two metric components separately; do not quote 10–40% or >30% without “across tested settings”; do not equate benchmark vote corruption with real-world harm.

canonical_title: The Trust Paradox in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems: When Collaboration Becomes a Security Vulnerability
canonical_authors: Zijie Xu; Minfeng Qi; Shiqing Wu; Lefeng Zhang; Qiwen Wei; Han He; Ningran Li
canonical_venue: IEEE Transactions on Computational Social Systems
version_status: Published IEEE journal metadata; technical full text available as arXiv 2510.18563.
identity_verdict: Canonical title/authors/DOI match the IEEE-linked record and arXiv version. Final IEEE pagination should still be added when available.
scope_rationale: The paper mixes ordinary over-sharing and malicious requests; confidentiality/authorization claims are security-relevant, but not every trust-utility result is an attack claim.
multiagent_verdict: Yes. Risk is defined over trust-conditioned cross-role requests and disclosures between separately instantiated role agents across closed-loop interaction chains.
adversary_position: Peer/requester agent operating through normal inter-agent channels; scenarios include ordinary, emergent, and overtly malicious requests.
adversary_capabilities: Issue contextually plausible requests and exploit elevated trust; no weight, orchestration, or infrastructure compromise.
preconditions: Parameterized trust changes disclosure behavior; Minimum Necessary Information labels are treated as the authorization reference.
mechanism: Trust-conditioned over-exposure: increased trust weakens cross-role information gates and permits requests beyond the MNI baseline.
attack_surfaces: Inter-agent requests; trust policy; cross-role information boundary; optional guardian.
primary_system_failure: Cross-principal confidentiality and authorization-boundary failure.
reported_impact: Disclosure beyond the MNI reference and trust-sensitive authorization drift in synthetic scenario chains.
agent_count_or_configuration: Role-based requester/holder interactions, optionally with a guardian; 1,488 chains across 19 sub-scenes, not 1,488 agents.
topology: Short closed-loop role interactions under AutoGen, LangGraph, and AgentScope.
communication: Text requests and responses conditioned on low/medium/high trust.
baselines: MNI reference, no defense, Sensitive Information Repartitioning, Guardian-Agent enablement, trust-level sweeps.
metric_definition: Task success, Over-Exposure Rate (MNI boundary violations), and Authorization Drift (sensitivity/slope across trust levels).
unit_denominator: Interaction-chain and disclosure-opportunity level as defined by the scenario/MNI labels; do not treat OER or AD as ordinary ASR.
system_level_impact_verified: Policy-label violation is verified in the synthetic environment; no real organization, tool execution, or persistent shared-memory impact is tested.
evidence_locators: ArXiv full text Sec. 3 pp. 3-4 Eqs. 2-4; Sec. 4 pp. 4-5 Tables I-III; Sec. 5 pp. 6-10 Figs. 4-9.
author_claim_vs_corpus_interpretation: Authors define a trust-vulnerability trade-off and two metrics. The corpus interpretation maps the observed exposure to confidentiality/authorization and treats trust as a design/precondition variable, not a failure category.

key_corrections: Reclassify primary from attack to evaluation; downgrade whole-paper scope to security_relevant while retaining core-security claim records for malicious over-exposure; separate OER/AD units; add final IEEE pages when available.

canonical_title: Prompt Infection: LLM-to-LLM Prompt Injection within Multi-agent Systems
canonical_authors: Donghyun Lee; Mo Tiwari; Brando Miranda

primary_system_failure: Compromise propagation and containment failure.
reported_impact: Population infection plus scenario-specific confidentiality, content-integrity, scam, malware, and action impacts.
agent_count_or_configuration: Role-specialized workflow chains and random pairwise societies of 10–50 agents.
topology: Global-history and local/predecessor messaging workflows; random pairwise population interactions.
communication: Text payload copied and adapted across downstream messages.

canonical_title: LLM-based Multi-Agents System Attack via Continuous Optimization with Discrete Efficient Search
canonical_authors: Weichen Yu; Kai Hu; Tianyu Pang; Chao Du; Min Lin; Matt Fredrikson
version_status: Published COLM 2025 conference paper on OpenReview; no DOI recorded.
identity_verdict: Title/authors match the repository’s published OpenReview record and COLM accepted-paper metadata; exact proceedings pagination is unavailable.
scope_rationale: The main claim is interaction-dependent self-replication and failure of compromise containment.
multiagent_verdict: Yes. A one-time intervention produces a suffix that is re-emitted through subsequent inter-agent messages, making compromise a multi-hop collective property.
adversary_position: External adversary able to intervene once against one agent/message.
adversary_capabilities: Optimize and inject a token-level suffix; no continuing control after the initial intervention.
preconditions: Agents exchange generated text and retain sufficient context for the suffix to be copied or regenerated downstream.
mechanism: CODES continuous-space token optimization plus discrete coordinate search for a self-repeating adversarial suffix.
attack_surfaces: Initial prompt/message; retained conversation context; inter-agent message chain; composed safeguard pipeline.
primary_system_failure: Compromise propagation and containment failure.
reported_impact: One seed affects later agents or multiple safeguard stages and induces harmful output; impact is demonstrated in three defined attack scenarios.
agent_count_or_configuration: One initially attacked agent followed by multiple recipients; configuration varies by scenario and should not be summarized as a single population size.
topology: Message-chain and composed safeguard configurations used in the three scenarios.
communication: Textual downstream propagation through retained context.
baselines: GCG, ADC, and other token-level optimization baselines; multi-level safeguards.
metric_definition: Attack success, self-repetition/propagation success, optimization loss, and optimization efficiency.
unit_denominator: Scenario/run and generated-message level; no single standardized population denominator is reported across all scenarios.

evidence_locators: Published PDF Abstract/Introduction pp. 1-2; threat scenarios throughout Sec. 2; method Sec. 3.2 p. 5 Algorithms 1-2; result tables in evaluation section.
author_claim_vs_corpus_interpretation: Authors call CODES an MAS attack. Corpus interpretation maps optimization to mechanism and containment to the violated property; it should not be merged with population infection rates from different papers.
limitations_maturity: Peer-reviewed conference evidence, but selected topologies/models and scenario-specific metrics; no universal infection curve, open membership, or long-term recovery.
key_corrections: Keep attack-primary; preserve single-intervention constraint; do not infer population-scale epidemic behavior or compare its success directly with agent-fraction infection metrics.

version_status: arXiv v2 revised 29 December 2025; no peer-reviewed publication verified.
identity_verdict: Title, two authors, arXiv ID/version history, and preprint-only status verified.
scope_rationale: Shared tool/function supply chain, cross-agent propagation, and safety-critical joint trajectory depend on explicit role interaction.
multiagent_verdict: Yes. A poisoned shared function changes one specialized agent’s output and downstream agents consume the corrupted result in a driving pipeline.
adversary_position: Malicious or compromised shared function-library/tool provider.
adversary_capabilities: Add deceptive function descriptions and callable malicious tools; target selected agent roles.
preconditions: Agents trust text-described shared library entries and pass outputs downstream.
mechanism: Function-library/tool poisoning with direct and downstream cascade paths.
attack_surfaces: Shared tool metadata/function library; specialized-agent pipeline; downstream planning.
primary_system_failure: Communication/shared-artifact and joint trajectory/action-integrity failure.
reported_impact: Trajectory error and collision-rate increases in AgentDriver and AgentThink.
agent_count_or_configuration: Specialized pipelines in two systems; exact role count differs and should be extracted per architecture.
topology: Perception/memory/reasoning/planning pipeline.
communication: Tool outputs and agent-to-agent intermediate results.
baselines: GCG, AutoDAN, CPA, BadChain, AgentPoison, instruction/filter defenses.
metric_definition: L2 trajectory error, collision rate, and ASR thresholded at L2 error 3 or 6.
unit_denominator: Driving episodes/samples; ASR definition changes with the specified L2 threshold and must always include it.
system_level_impact_verified: Trajectory/collision metrics in nuScenes-derived evaluation, not live vehicle impact.
evidence_locators: ArXiv v2 Abstract/Sec. 1 pp. 1-2 Fig. 1; method pp. 2-4 Figs. 2-3; Sec. 5 pp. 6-8 Table 2/Figs. 5-6.
author_claim_vs_corpus_interpretation: Authors call it a function-library attack. Corpus should distinguish the initial artifact integrity failure from downstream trajectory impact and not call all propagation authority escalation.
limitations_maturity: Preprint only; two driving frameworks, nuScenes-derived tasks, threshold-sensitive ASR, synthetic malicious tools, no live vehicle, incomplete defenses.
key_corrections: Keep attack-primary; require ASR threshold in every numeric claim; separate tool-state integrity and trajectory impact; avoid real-world safety extrapolation.

canonical_title: OMNI-LEAK: Orchestrator Multi-Agent Network Induced Data Leakage
canonical_authors: Akshat Naik; Jay Culligan; Yarin Gal; Philip Torr; Rahaf Aljundi; Alasdair Paren; Adel Bibi
version_status: arXiv v2 revised 25 February 2026; no peer-reviewed publication verified.
identity_verdict: Title, seven-author page list, arXiv ID/version history, and preprint status verified. ArXiv’s condensed “by ... and 5 other authors” display is inconsistent with the seven names and should not be used for counting.
scope_rationale: Differential authority and cross-agent data flow are the central attack mechanism and failure.
multiagent_verdict: Yes. One indirect injection crosses a data agent, orchestrator, and separate notification agent with distinct tools/permissions to exfiltrate data.
adversary_position: External content adversary without insider implementation knowledge.
adversary_capabilities: Place indirect prompt injection in public data; wait for privileged user query; receive exfiltrated email.
preconditions: Orchestrator delegates to distinct SQL/data and notification agents; poisoned record is retrieved; per-agent access controls allow split capabilities.
mechanism: Indirect prompt injection followed by orchestrator-mediated delegated authority composition and exfiltration.
attack_surfaces: Public data; data-agent context; orchestrator planning; notification tool/email boundary.
primary_system_failure: Cross-principal confidentiality and delegation/authorization integrity failure.
reported_impact: Exact sensitive records delivered to attacker-specified email in synthetic enterprise workflow.
agent_count_or_configuration: One orchestrator, SQL/data agent, notification agent; appendices include variants.
topology: Central orchestrator with specialized workers.
communication: Delegated natural-language/tool workflow and data returned to orchestrator/notification agent.
baselines: Direct and indirect attack variants; per-agent access control; model/database/query variations.
metric_definition: Strict exact-match end-to-end attack success plus benign task correctness.
unit_denominator: Workflow attack instances/queries; success requires correct sensitive content at correct attacker recipient, so partial or wrong-recipient cases are failures.
system_level_impact_verified: End-to-end synthetic email exfiltration is verified; no production database/email service.
evidence_locators: ArXiv v2 Abstract p. 1; Sec. 4.1 pp. 3-4 Figs. 2-3; Sec. 4.2 p. 4 Fig. 4; Sec. 5 pp. 4-7 Tables 1-5.
author_claim_vs_corpus_interpretation: Authors demonstrate access control does not compose into end-to-end noninterference. Corpus should avoid saying “all agents compromised” unless the paper’s role-specific criteria are met.
limitations_maturity: Preprint; synthetic employee database/email API, fixed orchestrator pattern, five frontier model families, strict metric, no complete defense or real deployment.
key_corrections: Keep attack-primary/core; label preprint; preserve exact success predicate; clarify agent count and seven-author list; do not generalize to all orchestrator MAS.

canonical_title: From Shield to Target: Denial-of-Service Attacks on LLM-Based Agent Guardrails
canonical_authors: Yuguang Zhou; Xunguang Wang; Pingchuan Ma; Zhantong Xue; Zhaoyu Wang; Shuai Wang
version_status: arXiv v2 revised 16 June 2026; no peer-reviewed publication verified.
identity_verdict: Title, six authors, arXiv ID/version history, and preprint status verified.
scope_rationale: Shared-monitor resource isolation is interaction-amplified, but the underlying guardrail DoS is not MAS-native and MAS is only one of several deployment evaluations.
multiagent_verdict: Partially. The attack primitive targets any reasoning guardrail; MAS-specific harm arises when co-located agents share the saturated guardrail and experience head-of-line blocking/starvation.
adversary_position: External content adversary whose payload is read and evaluated by runtime guardrail.
adversary_capabilities: Inject natural-language content optimized to extend guardrail reasoning; no guardrail code or agent control.
preconditions: Guardrail is on action-critical path and shared among agents; scheduling/resource limits allow one request to block others.
mechanism: Schema-shaped/optimized reasoning-extension payload causing guardrail token and latency amplification.
attack_surfaces: Untrusted content; shared guardrail service; scheduling/queue; timeout policy.
primary_system_failure: Shared-service availability and resource-isolation failure.
reported_impact: 13–63× token amplification in standalone tests, up to 148× latency in end-to-end deployments, and starvation/head-of-line blocking in shared MAS guardrail setting.
agent_count_or_configuration: Co-located agents sharing guardrail in MAS evaluation; exact count must be taken from Sec. 7.2/Table 10.
topology: Shared centralized guardrail bottleneck rather than agent communication graph.
communication: Agent requests pass through a common guardrail service; intermediate rewriting tested for payload resilience.
baselines: Prior reasoning-extension/adversarial methods, filters, token/time budgets, fail-open/fail-closed handling.
metric_definition: Generated tokens, latency amplification, throughput, blocked/task-success outcomes.
unit_denominator: Request/deployment-level resource ratios; amplification factors are ratios, not ASR or affected-agent fraction.
system_level_impact_verified: Shared-service starvation is shown in a controlled LangGraph-style deployment; no production outage.
evidence_locators: ArXiv v2 Abstract p. 1; Secs. 3-5 pp. 4-7 Fig. 1; Sec. 7.2 pp. 11-12 Table 10; conclusion p. 16.
author_claim_vs_corpus_interpretation: Authors present a general agent-guardrail DoS and a MAS deployment consequence. Corpus must not count it as interaction-unique or use standalone amplification as a MAS metric.
limitations_maturity: Preprint only; MAS is one of four deployments, centralized shared service, payload/scheduler configuration dependent, no production incident, defenses involve safety-availability trade-off.
key_corrections: Retain security_relevant rather than core; isolate MAS-specific starvation claim; separate token/latency ratios from ASR; do not label primitive unique to MAS.

canonical_title: AgentBreeder: Mitigating the AI Safety Risks of Multi-Agent Scaffolds via Self-Improvement
canonical_authors: J Rosser; Jakob Nicolaus Foerster
version_status: Published NeurIPS 2025 spotlight; canonical conference title differs from the earlier arXiv title “Mitigating the AI Safety Impact of Multi-Agent Scaffolds.”
identity_verdict: NeurIPS official program verifies the conference title, two authors, 2025 spotlight status, and the 79.4% abstract result. Use the conference title and merge arXiv:2502.00757 as the earlier version.
scope_rationale: The work evaluates safety properties of composed agent scaffolds and searches for unsafe configurations, but its primary evidence is benchmark safety under architecture search rather than a technical runtime security threat model.
secondary_roles: evaluation; automated system-design search; red-team safety probing
multiagent_verdict: Yes as a system-design study: the unit is a generated multi-agent scaffold composed of roles, prompts, and communication structure. It is not a runtime malicious-member attack study.
attack_role: red-mode discovers unsafe scaffolds; does not introduce a conventional adversary with a fixed foothold/capability model
adversary_position: No fixed external adversary. RedAgentBreeder optimizes scaffold designs under an inverted safety objective.
adversary_capabilities: Search over role prompts, agent programs, and communication/scaffold structures through evolutionary optimization.
preconditions: Safety and capability benchmarks are available as fitness objectives; generated scaffold behavior is evaluated end to end.
mechanism: Multi-objective evolutionary search can select either safer scaffolds or capability-preserving unsafe scaffolds.
attack_surfaces: System architecture; role prompts; communication/scaffold composition; evaluation objective.
primary_system_failure: Compositional safety degradation or reward-hacked safety behavior at the scaffold level.
reported_impact: Benchmark-level unsafe behavior in red mode and reported safety-score improvement in blue mode; not a demonstrated deployed compromise.
agent_count_or_configuration: Variable generated scaffolds; exact population sizes/configurations must be read from the individual discovered programs rather than summarized as one agent count.
topology: Automatically generated scaffold/program structures rather than one fixed topology.
communication: Defined by each generated scaffold and may include sequential or multi-agent exchanges.
baselines: Chain-of-thought, self-consistency, hand-designed scaffolds, and capability-only or safety-aware evolutionary objectives.
metric_definition: Safety benchmark score, capability benchmark score, Pareto performance, and helpfulness checks used to expose reward hacking.
unit_denominator: Benchmark-example and scaffold-level aggregate scores; “79.4% uplift” is a relative average benchmark improvement across three blue-mode runs, not attack success rate.
system_level_impact_verified: Only benchmark-level scaffold safety and capability effects are verified.
evidence_locators: NeurIPS official program abstract for publication identity and 79.4% result; conference paper Secs. 4–5 and result figures/tables for blue/red modes and reward hacking. Exact PDF locators remain for author signoff.
author_claim_vs_corpus_interpretation: Authors explicitly present blue and red evolutionary modes. Coding this as design-time prevention/evaluation rather than an attack-primary runtime paper is the corpus interpretation.
limitations_maturity: Peer-reviewed spotlight. Results depend on benchmark fitness, finite evolutionary budgets, generated scaffolds, and exhibit reward-hacking risk; safety-score uplift is not a security guarantee.
key_corrections: Use the NeurIPS title and spotlight venue; merge the earlier arXiv title; recategorize from mixed defense/attack to defense/evaluation primary; do not treat the 79.4% safety uplift as attack robustness or a guarantee.

canonical_title: AgentSafe: Safeguarding Large Language Model-based Multi-agent Systems via Hierarchical Data Management
canonical_authors: Junyuan Mao; Fanci Meng; Yifan Duan; Miao Yu; Xiaojun Jia; Junfeng Fang; Yuxuan Liang; Kun Wang; Qingsong Wen
version_status: arXiv v2, 8 July 2025; no archival venue verified.
identity_verdict: arXiv verifies title, nine-author order, submission history, v2 status, and arXiv DOI.
scope_rationale: The defense enforces inter-agent authorization and memory integrity, which require separately addressable agents and cross-agent information flow.
multiagent_verdict: Yes. Agent identities, authority levels, inter-agent messages, and shared/persistent memory are explicit security objects.
attack_role: evaluates unauthorized access, impersonation, and malicious-memory poisoning; does not primarily introduce a new attack
adversary_position: Unauthorized or impersonating member agent; malicious writer to shared memory.
adversary_capabilities: Request protected information, present false authority, or write poisoned content to shared memory.
preconditions: Agents and information are assigned hierarchical security labels; ThreatSieve and HierarCache are trusted enforcement components.
mechanism: Authority-aware message filtering and hierarchical memory management are tested against unauthorized requests, impersonation, and poisoning.
attack_surfaces: Inter-agent communication; identity/authority metadata; shared memory.
primary_system_failure: Cross-principal confidentiality and shared-state integrity failure.
reported_impact: Unauthorized disclosure or downstream influence from poisoned memory in the evaluated scenarios.
agent_count_or_configuration: Varied in scalability experiments; exact counts should be copied from the paper tables rather than inferred from the abstract.
topology: Role/authority-stratified collaboration; no single topology should be coded without checking the experiment table.
communication: Messages are screened using sender/receiver authority and information sensitivity.
baselines: Unprotected systems, component ablations, and prior prompt or memory defenses as specified in the paper.
metric_definition: Defense success rate under adversarial scenarios, task utility, and scalability measures.
unit_denominator: Attack-scenario/trial level; the abstract’s “above 80%” is an aggregate defense success statement, not a universal guarantee.
system_level_impact_verified: Yes for synthetic unauthorized-access and poisoning scenarios; no production deployment impact is established.
evidence_locators: arXiv abstract for two-component design and >80% headline; paper Sec. 3 framework and Sec. 4 experiments. Exact table/page locators require author signoff against v2 PDF.
author_claim_vs_corpus_interpretation: The authors explicitly claim hierarchical data and memory defense. Stable identity, correct labels, and trusted policy enforcement as the security contract are corpus interpretations from the design.
limitations_maturity: Preprint only. Relies on predefined security labels, stable identities, trusted enforcement, and evaluated task/model settings; dynamic membership and adaptive Sybils are not established.
key_corrections: Keep as defense-primary; record v2/preprint status; do not call it the first systematic memory defense without qualification; make policy-label and identity assumptions explicit; do not generalize the >80% figure.

canonical_title: An Adversary-Resistant Multi-Agent LLM System via Credibility Scoring
canonical_authors: Sana Ebrahimi; Mohsen Dehghankar; Abolfazl Asudeh
version_status: Published archival conference paper, December 2025.
identity_verdict: ACL Anthology verifies title, three-author order, proceedings, year, pages, and DOI.
scope_rationale: The protected property and defense are defined over adversarial member contributions and multi-agent aggregation.
multiagent_verdict: Yes. Persistent agent identities communicate iteratively and credibility-weighted aggregation changes the collective output.
attack_role: evaluates adversarial and low-performing members but does not primarily propose an attack
adversary_position: Adversarial or persistently unreliable member agents in iterative question answering.
adversary_capabilities: Submit misleading answers/contributions through the normal collaboration protocol.
preconditions: Agent identity persists across queries; past contribution quality can be scored; the credibility updater and aggregator are trusted.
mechanism: Historical credibility scores attenuate the influence of agents whose prior contributions were judged poor.
attack_surfaces: Member contributions; identity/history state; collective aggregation.
primary_system_failure: Collective decision-integrity failure under adversarial member influence.
reported_impact: Reduced answer accuracy under adversarial populations and empirical recovery from credibility-weighted aggregation.
agent_count_or_configuration: Varies by experimental population ratio; exact n and adversarial counts should be extracted per experiment.
topology: Iterative communication and centralized credibility-weighted aggregation.
communication: Agents communicate answers/contributions over repeated queries; historical state links identity to past quality.
baselines: Standard/unweighted aggregation and credibility-scoring variants.
metric_definition: Final task accuracy/robustness by adversarial population ratio; credibility values and related ablations.
unit_denominator: Question/task-instance level aggregated over experimental sets. “Adversary-majority” is an empirical task-accuracy condition, not Byzantine agreement.
system_level_impact_verified: Yes for benchmark collective-answer integrity; no protocol-level agreement/termination guarantee.
evidence_locators: ACL Anthology metadata and abstract; published PDF Secs. 2–4 for scoring, Sec. 5/results tables for adversarial ratios. Exact table locators require author signoff.
author_claim_vs_corpus_interpretation: Authors explicitly report resilience even in adversary-majority settings. The statement that this is not classical Byzantine agreement is the corpus interpretation required to prevent assumption drift.
limitations_maturity: Peer-reviewed. Requires stable identities, repeated-task histories, and a trusted quality signal; identity churn, Sybils, colluding reputation manipulation, and asynchronous agreement are not established.
key_corrections: Make defense the primary category; encode stable identity and trusted scoring as assumptions; do not compare the adversary-majority task result to f/n Byzantine thresholds or call it a consensus guarantee.

canonical_title: Audit the Whisper: Detecting Steganographic Collusion in Multi-Agent LLMs
canonical_authors: Om Tailor
version_status: arXiv v2, 17 October 2025; no archival peer-reviewed venue verified.
identity_verdict: arXiv verifies title, sole author, v2 date, subject categories, and arXiv DOI.
scope_rationale: The defense, benchmark, and failure are inherently multi-party: colluding agents exploit a hidden communication channel and an auditor observes/intervenes.
multiagent_verdict: Yes. Covert coordination is defined among communicating agents relative to an auditor and evaluated across collusion settings.
attack_role: instantiates/evaluates collusion channels drawn from several suites; primary novelty is auditing/detection
adversary_position: Colluding member agents sharing a covert textual scheme.
adversary_capabilities: Encode coordination signals in ordinary messages and adapt behavior to the allowed channel.
preconditions: Auditor can observe transcripts/outcomes and perform paired interventions, paraphrasing, rate limits, or role permutations; some fairness analysis assumes subgroup labels.
mechanism: Paired-run KL and mutual-information diagnostics, permutation/watermark/fairness signals, and calibrated union testing detect or constrain collusion.
attack_surfaces: Natural-language communication; auditor intervention; outcome/fairness signals.
primary_system_failure: Oversight and collective-decision integrity failure through steganographic collusion.
reported_impact: Detection power and false-positive-controlled auditing on ColludeBench and external collusion suites; not universal detectability.
agent_count_or_configuration: Pairs and groups vary by benchmark scenario; record per benchmark rather than one universal n.
topology: Communication scenarios in pricing, auctions, peer review, and imported external suites.
communication: Configurable covert schemes over textual channels; paired interventions modify channel capacity.
baselines: Heuristic transcript/outcome detectors and external suites including Secret Collusion/CASE/Perfect Collusion Benchmark/SentinelAgent as stated by the authors.
metric_definition: Detection power at a fixed 10^-3 false-positive budget, mutual-information/KL diagnostics, permutation invariance, watermark variance, fairness-aware acceptance bias, and e-value calibration.
unit_denominator: Run- or paired-run level over benchmark scenarios, including 10,000 honest runs for calibration according to the abstract.
system_level_impact_verified: Yes for benchmark detection and auditing outcomes; no deployment-wide guarantee against arbitrary covert channels.
evidence_locators: arXiv abstract for contributions, 10^-3 FPR, 10k honest runs, and external-suite evaluation; paper Secs. 5–6 and results/limitations for benchmark and detectors. Exact pages/tables require author signoff.
author_claim_vs_corpus_interpretation: Authors explicitly present capacity analysis and calibrated detectors. Coding trusted interventions, subgroup labels, and observer access as assumptions is the corpus interpretation of its defense contract.
limitations_maturity: Preprint only. Detection is task/channel dependent and relies on paired interventions, transcript/outcome visibility, calibration data, and in some analyses subgroup annotations.
key_corrections: Keep as defense/benchmark primary, not attack; record preprint status; code attack instances as secondary evidence; do not claim covert collusion is generally detectable or that finite-sample guarantees cover arbitrary channels.

canonical_title: BlockA2A: Towards Secure and Verifiable Agent-to-Agent Interoperability
canonical_authors: Zhenhua Zou; Zhuotao Liu; Lepeng Zhao; Qiuyang Zhan
version_status: arXiv v3, 21 September 2025; no archival peer-reviewed venue verified.
identity_verdict: arXiv verifies title, four-author order, v3 history, subjects, and arXiv DOI.
scope_rationale: The proposed framework addresses identity, message integrity, authorization, Byzantine members, and incident response across explicit A2A interactions.
secondary_roles: protocol/system design; threat analysis; prototype evaluation
multiagent_verdict: Yes. Cross-domain agent identities, signed interactions, delegated permissions, task state, and accountability are first-class protocol objects.
attack_role: evaluates several attack classes under the proposed protocol; does not primarily introduce a new attack
adversary_position: Byzantine or Sybil member, message/prompt tamperer, or compromised protocol participant.
adversary_capabilities: Spoof identity, equivocate, tamper with task messages/state, abuse delegated permissions, or submit adversarial prompts.
preconditions: All participating agents adopt DIDs, signatures, contracts, ledgers, policy oracles, and the Defense Orchestration Engine; ledger and cryptographic assumptions hold.
mechanism: Protocol-native identity, signed messaging, ledger provenance, context-aware smart-contract access control, reputation, revocation, and execution halting.
attack_surfaces: Discovery/identity; A2A messages; task contracts; delegation; shared task state; incident-response control plane.
primary_system_failure: Authentication, message/task integrity, authorization, provenance, and accountability failure.
reported_impact: Prototype-level attack neutralization and sub-second overhead under the framework’s ledger and oracle assumptions.
agent_count_or_configuration: Prototype cross-domain participants; exact n varies by experiment and is not a central population metric.
topology: A2A interactions mediated by decentralized identity and blockchain-anchored records.
communication: Signed protocol messages and task events recorded/verified through the proposed trust stack.
baselines: Legacy/non-ledger A2A security mechanisms and undefended attack scenarios as specified by the paper.
metric_definition: Attack-handling outcomes plus latency, throughput, and storage overhead.
unit_denominator: Per attack scenario/protocol operation and system performance trial; not a Byzantine consensus threshold experiment.
system_level_impact_verified: Only prototype/protocol evaluation under its trusted infrastructure; no broad production guarantee.
evidence_locators: arXiv abstract for architecture, DOE, attack classes, and sub-second overhead; paper Secs. 3–6 for components and prototype tables. Exact locator validation remains for author signoff.
author_claim_vs_corpus_interpretation: Authors explicitly claim secure/verifiable interoperability and use “Byzantine” broadly. Treating cryptography, ledger consensus, oracles, and endpoint adoption as the trusted computing base, and refusing to read the work as a classical BFT proof, are corpus interpretations.
limitations_maturity: Preprint, broad integrated architecture, substantial trusted infrastructure, latency/privacy/governance/oracle assumptions, and evaluation within the authors’ prototype.
key_corrections: Keep defense/system primary; record v3 and preprint status; do not treat “guarantees” or Byzantine flagging as a classical consensus theorem; explicitly list ledger/oracle/endpoint adoption assumptions and avoid “first” claims without independent verification.

canonical_title: Byzantine-Robust Decentralized Coordination of LLM Agents
canonical_authors: Yongrae Jo; Chanik Park
version_status: arXiv v1, 20 July 2025; no archival peer-reviewed venue verified.
identity_verdict: arXiv verifies title, two authors, v1 date, subject categories, and arXiv DOI.
scope_rationale: The defense and claims directly concern malicious members, distributed aggregation, agreement/selection, and liveness in an LLM-agent protocol.
multiagent_verdict: Yes. Worker proposals, evaluator rankings, and correctness/latency under Byzantine participants are defined over decentralized agent coordination.
attack_role: evaluates arbitrary Byzantine proposals/votes; primary novelty is DecentLLMs coordination
adversary_position: Byzantine member agents among workers or evaluators.
adversary_capabilities: Submit arbitrary proposals/scores/votes and exploit leader dependence in baseline coordination.
preconditions: Synchronous authenticated communication, known participant set, and Byzantine fraction below the protocol’s stated bound.
mechanism: Leaderless concurrent proposal generation and Byzantine-robust evaluator aggregation/selective finalization.
attack_surfaces: Proposal generation; evaluator scoring/ranking; voting/aggregation; coordination rounds.
primary_system_failure: Collective decision integrity and coordination availability under Byzantine members.
reported_impact: Empirical task-quality and latency/round robustness under varied Byzantine fractions; not a universal agreement theorem.
agent_count_or_configuration: Varied participant counts and Byzantine fractions in simulations/tasks; preserve per-experiment n and f.
topology: Leaderless decentralized coordination with workers and evaluators; authenticated synchronous links.
communication: Concurrent proposals followed by independent evaluator scoring and aggregation.
baselines: Leader-based coordination and conventional voting/aggregation baselines.
metric_definition: Selected-answer task quality/accuracy, latency, number of rounds, and robustness as f/n varies.
unit_denominator: Task-instance and protocol-run level. Any f<n/2 statement is conditional on synchrony/authentication and the paper’s correctness definition.
system_level_impact_verified: Yes for simulated/benchmark coordination performance; classical agreement, validity, and termination under asynchronous conditions are not established.
evidence_locators: arXiv abstract for DecentLLMs and empirical claim; full paper threat model/theorems in pp. 3–7 and experiment tables. All formal statements require expert signoff against exact theorem text.
author_claim_vs_corpus_interpretation: Authors explicitly motivate leaderless Byzantine robustness. Mapping any claimed threshold to relaxed synchrony/authentication and distinguishing answer quality from strict Byzantine agreement are corpus interpretations.
limitations_maturity: Preprint only. Formal claim depends on synchronous authenticated network, bounded population, and paper-specific selection correctness; evaluation is task/simulation specific.
key_corrections: Keep defense-primary; never cite f<n/2 without synchrony, authentication, and correctness definition; do not compare directly with classical asynchronous f<n/3 or call task accuracy an agreement guarantee; require distributed-systems signoff.

canonical_title: Cowpox: Towards the Immunity of VLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
canonical_authors: Yutong Wu; Jie Zhang; Yiming Li; Chao Zhang; Qing Guo; Han Qiu; Nils Lukas; Tianwei Zhang
version_status: Published peer-reviewed ICML 2025 paper.
identity_verdict: PMLR verifies title, eight-author order, conference, volume, pages, and year.
scope_rationale: The defense is explicitly population-distributed and addresses infectious jailbreak spread across agent memory/communication.
multiagent_verdict: Yes. Both attack and cure samples propagate over a population of stateful VLM agents; containment and recovery are system-level quantities.
attack_role: uses infectious VLM-agent attack as the evaluated threat; primary novelty is immunity/recovery
adversary_position: External adversary seeding contagious multimodal jailbreak content.
adversary_capabilities: Introduce a malicious multimodal sample that enters one agent’s state and can be transmitted to others.
preconditions: Agents exchange or inherit state/content; defender can generate and distribute cure samples through population channels.
mechanism: Cure samples immunize agents before exposure and propagate distributed protection/recovery so defensive reproduction competes with infection.
attack_surfaces: Multimodal input; local state/memory; agent-to-agent transmission; population topology.
primary_system_failure: Compromise propagation and containment failure.
reported_impact: Population infection, immunity, and recovery outcomes under the evaluated models/topologies, plus theoretical robustness guarantees under stated assumptions.
agent_count_or_configuration: Networked populations varied by experiments; preserve each seed and population size from tables.
topology: Population/network propagation settings analyzed empirically and theoretically.
communication: Malicious and defensive samples spread through the same inter-agent/state channels.
baselines: No defense and non-propagating/local safety interventions.
metric_definition: Infection, immunization/recovery, expected spread, robustness bounds, and benign utility.
unit_denominator: Agent/population and propagation-run level; distinguish expected number of infections, infected fraction, recovery rate, and utility.
system_level_impact_verified: Yes for evaluated population compromise and recovery; real open-network deployment is not tested.
evidence_locators: PMLR abstract for defense concept and theoretical guarantee; published PDF Secs. 3–4 and theorem/result tables for exact conditions. Author signoff required for every bound and denominator.
author_claim_vs_corpus_interpretation: Authors explicitly call Cowpox a distributed defense with theoretical guarantees. Coding it as one of the corpus’s few recovery-oriented defenses is the corpus interpretation.
limitations_maturity: Peer-reviewed. Specialized VLM infection model, controlled distribution of cure samples, model/task/topology assumptions, and uncertain deployability in open networks.
key_corrections: Keep defense-primary and explicitly code prevention plus recovery; separate infection and recovery denominators; quote theoretical guarantees only with full model assumptions; do not generalize to arbitrary LLM-MAS or open populations.

canonical_title: Goal-Aware Identification and Rectification of Misinformation in Multi-Agent Systems
canonical_authors: Zherui Li; Yan Mi; Zhenhong Zhou; Houcheng Jiang; Guibin Zhang; Kun Wang; Junfeng Fang
version_status: arXiv v1, 31 May 2025; no archival venue verified.

scope_rationale: It evaluates intentional misinformation injection and downstream multi-agent task integrity, but much of the endpoint is task performance/toxicity rather than a formal CIA/authorization property.
multiagent_verdict: Yes. Misinformation moves through task-oriented inter-agent information flows and the defense uses the global task goal to identify and rectify messages.
attack_role: defines/evaluates misinformation injection variants but primary contribution is MisinfoTask plus ARGUS
adversary_position: Input-level or member-level misinformation injector.
adversary_capabilities: Insert persuasive false claims into messages that downstream agents consume.
preconditions: Task goal is available; a trusted LLM reviewer has sufficient knowledge/context to identify and rewrite false goal-relevant information.
mechanism: Goal-aware claim identification followed by rectification of messages before downstream use.
attack_surfaces: Inter-agent messages; task-decomposition information flow; reviewer/rectification layer.
primary_system_failure: Collective factual/task integrity failure from misinformation propagation.
reported_impact: Reported reduction in misinformation toxicity and improvement in task success under tested injection settings.
agent_count_or_configuration: Workflow-specific; exact agent counts must be extracted from MisinfoTask/system configurations.
topology: Task decomposition/message-passing workflows, not one universal graph.
communication: Messages carrying factual claims are reviewed and rewritten relative to the system goal.
baselines: Prompt defenses and misinformation-detection/rectification variants.
metric_definition: Misinformation toxicity, task success under attack, identification/rectification effectiveness, and utility.
unit_denominator: Task/scenario and message-claim level depending on metric; abstract reports average 28.17% toxicity reduction and 10.33% task-success improvement across evaluated attacks.
system_level_impact_verified: Yes for benchmark task/factual integrity; no deployed-world action or formal correctness guarantee.
evidence_locators: arXiv abstract for MisinfoTask/ARGUS and 28.17%/10.33% averages; paper Secs. 3–5 and result tables for exact metrics. Exact page/table validation remains for author signoff.
